the_critical_question.question: Does IVUS (intravascular ultrasound) or any intravascular acoustic technology already cover the space of passive acoustic emission monitoring of thrombus micro-fractures during thrombectomy?
the_critical_question.answer: NO — the deep search found NO patent or publication that covers this specific application.

category_1_IVUS_thrombus_characterizatio.mechanism: ACTIVE ultrasound imaging — sends pulse, receives echo
category_1_IVUS_thrombus_characterizatio.overlap_with_c5_x_ae: NONE — IVUS is active imaging; C5-X-AE is passive emission listening. Different physical mechanism.

category_2_sonothrombolysis.description: Using acoustic energy to break clots (therapeutic, not diagnostic)

category_2_sonothrombolysis.overlap_with_c5_x_ae: NONE — sonothrombolysis sends energy; C5-X-AE receives energy. Opposite direction.

the_key_distinction_that_preserves_novel.all_existing_intravascular_acoustic_tech: IVUS (send pulse, receive echo), sonothrombolysis (send waves to break clot), ultrasonic thrombectomy (send shear to emulsify) — ALL are active
the_key_distinction_that_preserves_novel.c5_x_ae_is_PASSIVE: Listen for acoustic emissions generated by the clot's own micro-fractures — NO energy is sent into the clot
the_key_distinction_that_preserves_novel.the_information_bottleneck: Current systems cannot observe the INTERNAL damage state of the clot. They can image the surface (IVUS), measure bulk properties (force/elasticity), or model fracture computationally. But they CANNOT directly measure the accumulation of micro-fractures that precedes bulk failure. Acoustic emission IS that measurement — it is the direct signal of micro-fracture events.
the_key_distinction_that_preserves_novel.why_this_is_a_structural_moat: An incumbent cannot replicate this by adding software to an existing IVUS or force-sensing system. Passive acoustic emission requires a DIFFERENT sensor (acoustic emission transducer, not ultrasound transducer) and a DIFFERENT signal processing approach (event detection, not imaging). This is a hardware + algorithm moat, not just a software moat.

the_candidate_specification.the_invention: A method and system for predicting thrombus fragmentation during mechanical thrombectomy by passively detecting acoustic emissions from micro-fractures within the thrombus.
the_candidate_specification.the_mechanism: As a thrombectomy device engages a clot, mechanical stress accumulates within the clot structure. Before bulk fracture occurs, micro-fractures accumulate and emit acoustic waves (acoustic emissions). These emissions are detectable by an acoustic emission sensor on or near the thrombectomy device. The rate, amplitude, and frequency spectrum of these emissions reveal the internal damage state of the clot, enabling prediction of impending fragmentation BEFORE it occurs.
the_candidate_specification.the_information_bottleneck_addressed: Current systems cannot observe the INTERNAL damage state of the clot. They can image the surface (IVUS), measure bulk properties (force), or model fracture computationally. But they CANNOT directly measure the accumulation of micro-fractures. Acoustic emission IS that direct measurement.
key_components: Acoustic emission sensor (piezoelectric or similar) integrated into or attached to thrombectomy device
Signal processing to detect and classify micro-fracture events
Predictive model relating AE event rate/spectrum to impending fragmentation risk
Real-time feedback to clinician (alert when fragmentation risk exceeds threshold)
why_this_is_better_than_existing_approac: IVUS: images clot surface but cannot detect internal micro-fractures. C5-X-Ae directly measures the fracture process.
Force/elasticity measurement: measures bulk mechanical properties but cannot detect micro-fracture accumulation. C5-X-AE detects individual fracture events.
Computational modeling: predicts fracture from geometry/properties but requires pre-procedure imaging and cannot adapt in real-time. C5-X-AE measures the actual fracture process in real-time.
Device motion ML (US 20250072970): infers clot properties from device motion. C5-X-AE directly measures clot internal state via its own acoustic emissions.

honest_disclosure.what_this_search_proves: C5-X-acoustic-emission survives the DEEP novelty search across 8 queries. No patent or publication covers this specific application. The candidate is ELIGIBLE for simulation under the simulation-budget-follows-novelty-confidence rule.
honest_disclosure.what_this_search_does_NOT_prove: This search does NOT prove the candidate is patentable. A formal freedom-to-operate analysis by a patent attorney, including full-text patent claim analysis and CNIPA/JPO search, is required before filing.
honest_disclosure.what_this_search_does_NOT_guarantee: This search does NOT guarantee the candidate will work. The acoustic emission from thrombus micro-fractures may be too weak to detect, too noisy to interpret, or too late to be actionable. These are SCIENTIFIC questions that require simulation and eventually physical experiment.
honest_disclosure.the_epistemic_discipline: The candidate has earned the right to consume simulation budget. It has NOT earned the right to enter the portfolio. That requires: (a) simulation success, (b) independent reproduction, (c) competitor superiority, (d) buyer moat, (e) full World-Class gate.
